Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: Ilwww.dilg.com. h DILG OPINION No. 39 s. 4023 15 2023 ANTONIO O. MASANGKAY konsimasangkay@gmail.com 0922 812 05 98 / 0922 841 4424 Dear Mr. Masangkay: This has reference to your letter dated February 27, 2023 to this Department requesting for a legal opinion regarding the terminal leave benefits of elected government public officials who have rendered service beyond the retirement age of 65 years old. Per your representations, the City Human Resource Management Office of the City of Antipolo has declined your request to the entitlement of the said benefit. Based on the Service Record submitted to this Office, from August 2011 to June 2013, you were appointed as Sangguniang Panlungsod member of the second district of Antipolo at the age of 67. From July 2013 to June 2022, you were further elected into Office and served for three (3) consecutive terms from the age of 69 until 78. For purposes of discussion, the Civil Service Commission (CSC) MC No. 14, s. 19991 provided the following regarding terminal leave: Sec. 35. Terminal Leave - terminal leave is applied for by an official or an employee who intends to sever his connection with his employer. Accordingly, the filling of application for terminal leave requires as a condition sine qua non, the employee's resignation, retirement or separation from the service. It must be shown first that public employment ceased by any of the said modes of severances. Sec. 37. Payment of Terminal Leave - any official/employee of the government who retires, voluntarily resigns or is separated from the service and who is not otheMise covered by special law, shall be entitled to the commutation of his leave credits exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and Holidays without limitation and regardless of the period when the credits were earned. I Additional Provisions and Amendments to CSC Memorandum Circular No. 41, 1998. Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Corollary thereto, the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) issued Circular Letter No. 2009-82, which clarified CSC MC No. 273 and reiterated the period of government service entitled to incentive, the pertinent portions are as follows: 2.1 Per CSC MC No. 27 dated 8 October 2001, the services rendered by a personnel who have reached the compulsory retirement age of 65 and are on extended service based on a CSC resolution shall no longer be credited as part of government service. Thus, personnel who are in this situation and whose position may be affected by the Rationalization Program are not entitled to avail of the Program Incentives since they are considered retired from government service. 2.2 Under the same CSC MC, the services rendered by personnel who have reached the compulsory retirement age of 65 and are on extended service for the purpose of completing the 15-year service requirement under the GSIS Law, shall be credited as part of government service, but only for a maximum period of one (I) year. xxx xxx xxx 2.3 Similarly, under said CSC MC and other jurisprudence on the matter, employees occupying coterminous/primarily confidential positions, and who reach the age of 65 years, are considered automatically extended in the service until the expiry date of their appointment or until their services are earlier terminated. The creditable service under automatic extension of service is only for a maximum period of one (1) year. xxx xxx 2.4 Pursuant to Sec. 14.b of the IRR of EO 366, only the government service up to age 59 and a fraction thereof, shall be counted for purposes of the incentive. Government service starting at the age of 60 shall no longer be subject to the incentive. [emphasis supplied] A closer scrutiny of the aforecited paragraphs would reveal whether the service rendered is part of government service or not, provided the requisites are present. According to Par 2.1, (1) personnel who have reached the compulsory retirement age of 65; and (2) on an extended service based on CSC resolution. Under this paragraph, they are considered retired from government service and shall not be deemed as part of government service. According to Par 2.2, the following are the requisites for the entitlement of terminal leave benefit: (1) personnel who have reached the compulsory retirement age of 65; (2) on extended service; and (3) for the purpose of completing the 15-year service requirement under the GSIS Law shall be entitled to a maximum period of one (1) year credit of government service. The same is also true for Par 2.3 which credits a maximum period one (1) year of service for persons who have reached the age of 65 while occupying 2 Clarification on the Availment of Incentives under EO No. 366 of Affected Personnel on Extended Service, March 9, 2009. 3 Amendments to section 12, Rule XII of CSC MC No. 15, s. 1999. Page 2 of 3

coterminous/primarily confidential positions until the expiry date of their appointment or until their services were terminated. Applying the foregoing to your case, the Department agrees with the City Human Resource Management Office of the City of Antipolo in declining your request to the entitlement of the said benefit as the two last requisites are not present: (1) you are no longer on the extended service; and (2) you have rendered only eleven (11) years of service. This opinion is without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities or courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. We hope to have enlighten you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY I OR R.
